title: Superflow vs Filestage
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS FILESTAGE · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Filestage is a proofing tool. Superflow is a QA tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more manual pass before launch.
qualifier: If your agency reviews client sites in Filestage, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Filestage hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Filestage's AI checks the files you upload. The live site still waits for a person.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: AI Review Agents scan uploaded files for typos, spelling, logos, and forbidden terms, Business plan and up, capped at 50 agent credits a month.
For live websites, a person reviews what loads at the URL.
dimensions.verdict: Filestage's agents catch mistakes in a file before a person opens it. Ours catch mistakes on the live site itself, the part a file can't show.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Reviewer groups per stage, due dates, automated reminders, one-click Approve or Request changes.
No account needed to review. On higher tiers, a Verified approval adds a signed, audit-ready sign-off.
dimensions.verdict: Filestage's approval workflow is as formal as ours. Call this one even: the difference shows up elsewhere, in what gets checked before the gate opens.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Half of client work lives behind a password.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: Live websites load by URL in real time. No saved history of past versions.
Private or authenticated sites need Filestage's IP addresses whitelisted, not a reviewer login.
dimensions.verdict: Filestage embeds a URL. Superflow reviews the site logged in, with SSO, no extension. Behind a password is where the gap shows.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Team-only comments keep discussion private between teammates and creatives, Starter plan and up.
dimensions.verdict: Both keep the argument away from the client. Even.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Timestamped annotations on video and audio, plus comments on images, documents, and live sites.
A screenshot saves automatically for each website comment. Other file types: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Filestage's annotations are detailed. Automatic screenshots on every comment type, and screen, video, and voice recordings: not yet verified on their side.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No project-wide memory concept verified. Agents use only the context you configure per project: brand guidelines, forbidden terms, uploaded compliance docs.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Jira, Monday, Slack, Teams, Zapier, Make, Adobe apps, and Google Drive folder sync, plus API and webhooks.
Jira and Monday push versions, due dates, and statuses out. Full two-way ticket sync: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Filestage pushes updates out to Monday and Jira. If a two-way board is your spine, weigh that honestly.

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Free EUR 0, Starter EUR 199, Business EUR 329 per month, Enterprise custom. 10 seats included, add-on bundles of 5. Reviewers are unlimited and free. AI Review Agents start on the Business plan.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open Filestage projects finish in Filestage. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Filestage's approval workflow is genuinely thorough. Reviewer groups, due dates, and reminders keep a review on schedule. Reviewers never need an account. It reviews video, images, documents, and live websites in one place, and its AI Review Agents catch typos and brand slips before a person opens the file.
stayLine: If your team's real need is gathering feedback and formal sign-off on creative files and assets, Filestage is a strong proofing tool. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Filestage with AI added?
faq.answer: No. Filestage's agents scan uploaded files for typos and brand slips. Superflow's agents check the live site itself, every change, and a person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Filestage projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in Filestage. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We also proof documents and video in Filestage.
faq.answer: Keep Filestage for that. Superflow reviews the live site: pages, forms, and flows a document can't show.
